name: Respawn Room
tagline: Ponnila College's e-sports and gaming society. Queue up, play fair, say GG.
about:
Respawn Room is the e-sports and gaming society of Ponnila College of Engineering in Kottayam. It started in 2022 in a hostel room with one borrowed router and six people who were tired of losing to each other's lag. Today we have a gaming lab of twenty-four PCs donated by alumni, about 260 members, and a reputation across central Kerala for running the cleanest college tournaments around.

We play a bit of everything: tactical shooters, mobile battle royale, football sims, fighting games, rapid chess and a surprisingly fierce weekly card-game night. We field college teams in inter-college leagues, run our own tournaments twice a semester, and host a game jam every year where people make games instead of only playing them.

Besides winning, we take two things seriously. The first is fair play: no smurfing, no cheats, no abuse on voice chat, and a code of conduct we actually enforce. The second is balance: the lab closes at 11 p.m. on weeknights, exam weeks are tournament-free, and there's a peer mentor for anyone whose gaming has started to hurt their grades.

Women gamers have their own Thursday lab slot and their own teams in two leagues, and this year they've won more trophies than the rest of us combined.

events.name: Respawn Cup Season 3: LAN Finals

venue.name: Respawn Room gaming lab, Ponnila College
venue.address: Ponnila College of Engineering, Kodimatha, Kottayam

events.about:
Sixteen teams of five from nine colleges, one day, one lab, and a 5v5 tactical shooter bracket that went to a 13-11 decider in the grand final. Season 3 was our biggest LAN yet: every match was played on identical machines on a wired network, with admins at every row and a live stream in Malayalam and English that peaked at 1,900 viewers.

The winners, from Kodamanju Institute of Technology in Idukki, took home the trophy and a month of free hours at Pixelpura Gaming Cafe. Our own women's team made the semi-finals in the open bracket, the first time a women's team has gone that far in the Cup. The fee covered lab hire, food all day and the finalists' jerseys.
events.guidelines: Teams check in by 9:30 with college IDs for all five players and one substitute. Bring your own mouse, keyboard and headset; monitors and PCs are provided and identical. Our code of conduct applies all day: no abuse on voice chat, no cheating software, no arguing with admins mid-round. Disputes go to Nabeel, whose decision is final.

speakers.name: Nabeel Ahammed
speakers.bio: Ran all thirty-one matches of the day without a single unresolved dispute, and only one raised voice, which was his own at the projector.

speakers.name: Abhay Varkey
speakers.bio: Casts college tournaments across Kerala in Malayalam and English, sometimes inside the same sentence.

speakers.name: Fidha Rahman
speakers.bio: Produced the full ten-hour stream from the lab corner and edited the highlight reel by midnight.

swag.name: A month of free hours for the winners

comments: Best-run college LAN I've played. Identical machines, no ping excuses.
The 13-11 grand final will be talked about for years.
Admins were fair and fast. Nobody felt cheated.
The lab got hot by the afternoon; more fans for next season, please.
Watching the women's team reach the semis was the highlight of the day.

events.name: Ponnila Game Jam 2026: Monsoon

venue.name: Respawn Room gaming lab and Seminar Hall 1
venue.address: Ponnila College of Engineering, Kodimatha, Kottayam

events.about:
Forty-eight hours to make a game, from Friday evening to Sunday evening, around one theme revealed at the opening: monsoon. Teams of one to four, any engine, any art style, and no experience needed. Several first-years made their first game ever.

Fourteen games were finished. Our favourites: a puzzle game about steering a paper boat through Kottayam's flooded streets, a rhythm game played on falling raindrops, and a very short horror game set on a night bus with a leaking roof. Gopika, an indie developer from Kochi, mentored teams all weekend and judged the final showcase.
events.guidelines: Any engine or framework is allowed; you must start the project after the theme is revealed. Pre-made assets are fine if they are free to use and credited. The lab stays open overnight with admins on rotation; sleeping bags are allowed in Seminar Hall 1. All games are shown at the Sunday showcase, finished or not.

events.name: Rapid Chess Open and Board Game Night

venue.name: College Canteen Hall, Ponnila College
venue.address: Ponnila College of Engineering, Kodimatha, Kottayam

events.about:
A break from screens. The first half of the evening was a seven-round rapid chess open, ten minutes plus five seconds a move, open to students, staff and anyone from Kottayam who turned up. The second half was board game night: Ludo, carrom, a Malayalam drawing-and-guessing game, and a strategy game a second-year brought back from Bengaluru that nobody fully understood but everyone enjoyed.

Forty-three players entered the chess open. Prof. Ranjith, our faculty advisor and the evening's favourite, lost in round two to a first-year from Civil, who went on to finish third. The canteen stayed open late and sold out of pazhampori by nine.
events.guidelines: Chess: bring your own board if you have one; clocks are provided. Touch-move applies. Phones off at the board. Board games: just turn up; tables are first come, first served. Please return every carrom coin you find on the floor.

speakers.name: Prof. Ranjith Mohan
speakers.bio: Organised the college's first chess club in 2015 and has been beaten by a first-year every year since.

speakers.name: Thomas Chummar
speakers.bio: Has arbitrated district chess tournaments in Kottayam for ten years and can spot a touch-move dispute from across the hall.

events.name: Women's Lab Night: Open Scrims

venue.name: Respawn Room gaming lab, Ponnila College
venue.address: Ponnila College of Engineering, Kodimatha, Kottayam

events.about:
Our Thursday women's lab slot, opened up to women gamers from every college in Kottayam. The first hour is practice scrims in mixed-skill teams, so complete beginners play alongside league players. The second hour is a short session from Shilpa, who started on these exact lab PCs as a first-year and now plays semi-professionally.

After that, the lab is yours: try any game installed, ask the women's team anything, or sign up for a spot on next semester's league roster. No experience needed and no judgement, ever.
events.guidelines: Open to women and non-binary students from any college; bring a college ID. Headsets are available, but bring your own if you have one. The lab's code of conduct applies, and our women's team admins run the evening.

speakers.name: Merlin Babu
speakers.bio: Led the women's team to two league titles this year and still plays support because nobody else wants to.

speakers.name: Shilpa Narayan
speakers.bio: Started on the Respawn Room lab PCs as a first-year and now plays for a women's team in a national league.

events.name: Royale Rumble: Inter-College Mobile Battle Royale
events.about:
Thirty squads of four from colleges across Kerala, four matches, one night, all on mobile. Points come from placement and eliminations, and the top eight squads go through to a LAN final at Pixelpura Gaming Cafe next semester.

Every match is streamed with Malayalam commentary by Fidha and Abhay. Squads play from wherever they are, with an admin in every lobby and a verified college ID for every player. Free to enter, because entry fees keep mobile players out more than anyone else.
events.guidelines: Register each player separately with the same squad name. Every player needs a verified college ID uploaded before the day. Emulators are not allowed; phones and tablets only. Lobby codes are shared thirty minutes before each match in the event chat. Teaming with other squads means instant disqualification.

speakers.name: Nabeel Ahammed
speakers.bio: Will be in every lobby with a stopwatch and the rulebook, and has already written the tie-break rules twice.

speakers.name: Fidha Rahman

events.name: Respawn Cup Season 4: LAN Finals

venue.name: Respawn Room gaming lab, Ponnila College
venue.address: Ponnila College of Engineering, Kodimatha, Kottayam

events.about:
The Respawn Cup is back for Season 4, and for the first time there are two brackets: an open bracket of twelve teams and a women's bracket of four, played side by side in the same lab on the same day. All sixteen team slots filled within a week of opening.

If you didn't get a slot, come and watch. Spectator seating in Seminar Hall 1 is free, with the matches on the big screen and Abhay and Fidha on commentary. The stream runs all day for anyone who can't make it to Kodimatha.
events.guidelines: Team registrations are closed. Registered teams check in by 9:30 with college IDs for every player. Bring your own peripherals; machines are identical and provided. Spectators: no registration needed, seating is first come, first served, and the code of conduct applies to the crowd too.

speakers.name: Athul Krishna
speakers.bio: Has played in every Respawn Cup and is organising this one instead, which he says is harder than any grand final.

speakers.bio: Back on the desk after casting the Season 3 grand final, and still hoarse from it.
